change.author: Alan

findings.title: Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws TypeError
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or `[]`. Line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without `?.`, which throws. The old code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. handleNewBooking can set `destinationCalendar: null` (handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067), and the other handlers now pass `[]`. Every booking whose location is Google Meet and which has no destination calendar will crash in `EventManager.create` instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Fallback lookup compares externalId to itself and never matches
findings.body: This branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` then compares against a falsy value, so it returns `undefined` for any real destination calendar. The old fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. In `updateEvent`, `calendarId` becomes `undefined` and `events.update` fails for references stored without `externalCalendarId`. Legacy references have none, and the non-credentialId create path also stores none (see the EventManager.ts:376 finding). The same bug is in `deleteEvent` at lines 315-317, where it silently falls back to `primary` instead of the destination calendar. Fall back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` (or the first destination) instead.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId when insert fell back to "primary"
findings.body: The insert uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` (line 154). The follow-up `events.patch` still passes the raw `selectedCalendar`, which is `undefined` whenever no destination matches this credential. Before the change `selectedCalendar` was always `"primary"` or an externalId. The patch that writes the Meet link into the description now fails, with no callback or log. Compute `const calendarId = selectedCalendar || "primary"` once and use it for both calls.

findings.title: Destination calendars without a credentialId lose their externalId and calendar target
findings.body: For a destination with no `credentialId`, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without `externalId` (line 380). Google's `createEvent` picks its calendar with `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, which never matches a destination whose `credentialId` is null. The event is therefore created on `primary` rather than on the destination's `externalId`, which the old code used. The returned result has `externalId` undefined, so the stored reference has `externalCalendarId` unset (line 169). Later updates and deletes then cannot find the right calendar (see the Google `updateEvent` finding). Pass `destination.externalId` here, and make Google match on `credentialId` or on `integration`.

findings.title: Non-Google calendars ignore the new credentialId and always use the first destination
findings.body: `Calendar.createEvent` now takes `credentialId`. EventManager creates one event per destination, with a different credential for each team member on collective events. Only Google uses `credentialId`. Office365 here, Lark (larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128-129) and the CalDAV base class (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163) all take `event.destinationCalendar[0]`. A collective member whose calendar is one of these creates the event on the first host's calendar id. `EventManager` meanwhile records `destination.externalId` of the member as the reference's `externalCalendarId`, so the stored reference is wrong. Select the destination by `credentialId` in these services too, or document that team destination calendars only work for Google.

findings.title: updateLocation now writes references with no externalCalendarId or credentialId
findings.body: `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (CalendarManager.ts:313-322) returns no `externalId` or `credentialId`, and the new `externalId` is only set by `createEvent`. `updateLocation` previously filled these from `evt.destinationCalendar`. Now `result.externalId` is undefined and `result.credentialId ?? undefined` is undefined for calendar results. editLocation.handler.ts:120 does `references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`, so a calendar reference with `uid ""`, no credentialId and no externalCalendarId is added next to the original one. handleCancelBooking now iterates every calendar reference, not just the first. On cancel, the junk reference takes the no-credentialId branch and calls `deleteEvent("", ...)` on every calendar credential. Return `externalId` and `credentialId` from `updateEvent`, or do not create references for update results.

findings.title: Error in updateAllCalendarEvents is no longer logged
findings.body: The `console.error(message)` call was removed, so `message` is built and never used. Any exception in this method is turned into silent `success: false` results with no log. The method now also makes DB lookups (`prisma.credential.findUnique`) and loops over several references, so there are more ways to throw. Restore the log, preferably with `log.error`.

findings.title: updateEvent can be called with an undefined credential
findings.body: When the credential is not in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup returns nothing, or returns a credential whose `app.slug` is null, `credential` stays undefined, or keeps the previous loop iteration's value because it is declared outside the loop. `updateEvent(credential, ...)` then dereferences it (`credential.appName`, CalendarManager.ts:314). The throw is caught and every reference is reported as failed with no log. Skip the reference, and log, when no credential is found. The same pattern, with a silent skip, is in createAllCalendarEvents at lines 356-374.

findings.title: Recurring cancel repeats the whole delete block once per calendar reference
findings.body: The `recurringEvent && recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings` branch (lines 444-468) now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. It iterates all of the user's calendar credentials and every updated booking, and does not use `reference`. With N calendar references on a booking, it runs N times, so the same events are deleted N times. Duplicate Google deletes return 410 and are swallowed, but other providers may reject. Hoist the recurring branch out of the loop so it runs once. In the same loop, the no-credentialId branch (line 473 onward) now repeats for each legacy reference.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite drops `organization` from dynamic users and changes error behaviour
findings.body: (1) The dynamic-user `select` (lines 731-740) no longer includes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. The host query at lines 321-325 still includes it and `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) requires it, so dynamic-group bookings lose the field. This will probably break the type check, or leave `organization` undefined at runtime for downstream code. (2) An empty `dynamicUserList` now throws, which the catch turns into a 500 "Unable to load users", where before the query returned `[]`. (3) The catch rewraps every `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` as a 400 carrying the raw Prisma message, which is returned to the booker. The `HttpError` branch also overwrites the original status code. None of this is related to destination calendars. Revert this part, or at least keep the `organization` select.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer/event type has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (lines 1063-1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so collective members' calendars are ignored. Build the array first (`[own, ...teamDestinationCalendars].filter(Boolean)`). Also, only `destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the booking (line 1877), so the other members' destination calendars are not recorded on the booking row. Cancel and reschedule rebuild `destinationCalendar` from that single column.

findings.title: Unrelated refactors mixed into the destinationCalendar change
findings.body: The change also includes the `isTeamEventType` rewrite (line 689) and the `orginalBookingDuration` rename. It adds a `firstName`/`lastName` placeholder to team members. It changes `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {slug}` in organizations/create.handler.ts, and the notes string "organiser" to "organizer" in CalendarManager.ts:230. These widen the blast radius of a risky refactor. Split them out. The `teamMemberPromises` callback also pushes to the outer `teamDestinationCalendars` array as a side effect inside `map`. It works only because the push happens before the first `await`, so build the array synchronously instead.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changes from object to array
findings.body: `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is serialized into webhook payloads. It changes from an object to an array for every consumer, while the null case is kept in some places and becomes `[]` in others. For example webhook.e2e.ts:119 and :373 still expect `null`, while :249 expects `[]`. This is a breaking change for webhook subscribers and Zapier/Make templates. Make the empty value consistent (null vs `[]`) and note the change for webhook consumers.

findings.title: Test coverage for the new multi-destination behaviour is missing
findings.body: Only the BOOKING_REJECTED fixture was adjusted. No test covers collective events with several destination calendars, the DB credential fallback in createAllCalendarEvents/updateAllCalendarEvents, multi-reference cancel, or the Google Meet fallback with no destination calendar (which would have caught the TypeError at EventManager.ts:119).

contracts.action: EventManager.create: Google Meet fallback check on evt.destinationCalendar[0]
contracts.before_after: Before: null-safe optional chaining on the object. After: destructures first array element and dereferences without `?.`.
contracts.visible_effect: Booking with Google Meet location and no destination calendar fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError thrown inside EventManager.create; booking creation errors.

contracts.action: createAllCalendarEvents: one event per destination calendar, credential fetched from DB when not in organizer credentials
contracts.equivalent_path: Old single-destination logic using destinationCalendar.credentialId, or integration filter
contracts.before_after: Before: one createEvent call for the one destination, externalId stored from destinationCalendar. After: loop over destinations; credentialId branch passes destination.externalId, integration branch passes none; non-credentialId branch loses externalCalendarId.
contracts.visible_effect: Collective team members get events on their calendars (Google only matches by credentialId); legacy destinations go to primary and store no externalCalendarId.
contracts.failure_mode: createEvent errors are swallowed in CalendarManager (success false); a missing credential in the DB is silently skipped.

contracts.action: handleCancelBooking: delete events for every calendar reference, with DB credential fallback
contracts.equivalent_path: Old code deleted only the first calendar reference (`.find`) and used booking user credentials only
contracts.before_after: After: loop over references; recurring-delete block is nested inside the loop and repeats per reference; legacy references loop over all credentials per reference. Failures from apiDeletes are awaited at 619/656.
contracts.visible_effect: Duplicate deletes for recurring bookings; junk references (uid "") created by editLocation are now also processed on cancel.
contracts.failure_mode: deleteEvent rejection on providers that don't swallow 404/410 could fail the cancellation.

contracts.action: editLocation → EventManager.updateLocation writes referencesToCreate from update results
contracts.equivalent_path: createEvent path, which does return externalId/credentialId
contracts.before_after: Before: externalCalendarId/credentialId taken from evt.destinationCalendar. After: taken from results, which CalendarManager.updateEvent does not populate.
contracts.visible_effect: Booking gets an extra calendar reference without credentialId/externalCalendarId.
contracts.failure_mode: Later cancel or reschedule processes the junk reference.

summary: The calendar changes turn `destinationCalendar` into an array, and several call sites were not converted correctly. One blocker: `EventManager.create` dereferences the first destination calendar without `?.`, so a Google Meet booking with no destination calendar throws a TypeError. The Google service's fallback lookup compares `externalId` to the falsy `externalCalendarId` it is already known to be missing, so it never matches. Legacy destinations with no `credentialId` lose their `externalCalendarId`. `updateLocation` now stores calendar references with no credential or external id. Recurring cancel repeats the delete block once per reference. `loadUsers` was rewritten with side effects unrelated to the PR. I did not run anything; this is from reading the code.
